objective: P2 Stage 2 (plan v2 section 3.2): reproduce the statistical jump model regime strategy (Shu-Yu-Mulvey 2024) on the US market 1990-2023, sweep nine specifications along inputs, persistence and model class, and test whether the daily regime multiplier raises the exposure-matched Sharpe of the pilot sleeve S3 in the stress window without costing more than 0.10 of recent Sharpe; S1, S2 and C2 are reported.

parameters.model: statistical jump model, 2 states, loss 0.5 * squared Euclidean distance, jump penalty on every state change, coordinate descent with k-means++ starts (n_init 10, fixed seeds, max_iter 1000, tol 1e-8) as in the jumpmodels package; online inference = forward pass values[t] = loss[t] + min_j(values[t-1][j] + lambda * 1{j != k}) started 3000 sessions before each refit date with that refit's parameters and run forward to the next refit; state_t = argmin_k values[t]
parameters.features: F3: EWM downside deviation (halflife 10) and EWM Sortino ratios (halflives 20 and 60) of the market excess return, each EWM computed with the given halflife on daily data (Shu-Yu-Mulvey 2024 section 3.3)
parameters.jump_penalty: CV over {0, 5, 15, 35, 50, 70, 100, 150}; cross-validated: at the first session of each month choose the value maximising the Sharpe of the index 0/1 strategy (one-day delay, 10 bp) over the trailing 2016 sessions (8 years) of that value's own online sequence; the choice applies from session t+2
parameters.role: paper base specification and reproduction target
parameters.market_series: daily excess return: French F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily Mkt-RF (CRSP value-weighted) 1970-01-02..2015-12-31; SPY SIP adjusted close-to-close return minus RF from 2016-01-04; RF = French daily RF through its last date, then the mean daily RF of its last month
parameters.fit: refit on the first session of January and July on the trailing 3000 sessions; each feature clipped at training mean +/- 3 sd, then z-scored with the training mean and sd (jumpmodels example pipeline); states sorted by cumulative market excess return in the training window (jumpmodels sort_by cumret), bull = higher
parameters.multiplier_timing: state inferred at close d sets the multiplier from session d+2 (one-day delay, paper protocol); zero-delay (from d+1) is report-only
parameters.index_level: 0/1 strategy on the market series: in-market sessions earn excess + rf, out-of-market sessions earn rf; 10 bp per unit change of the multiplier
parameters.sleeves: S1, S2 and S3 at offsets 0,4,8,12,16 (S3 with the frozen vol target 0.40 and dip boost 0.60 for 10 sessions), C2 at o00; frozen engines through reports/research/program/etf-open-close-2026-10-07/compute.py simulate_effective; risky weights times m, the remainder in the sleeve's own cash asset; 10 bp per side on traded notional
parameters.control_vt: exposure-matched volatility target: m_VT = min(1, tau / sigma_hat), sigma_hat = EWM (halflife 21 sessions) annualised volatility of the ungated object's daily net return known at close d, applied with the same delay; tau by bisection so that mean(m_VT) equals mean(m_spec) within each window (per offset for sleeves)
parameters.placebo: circular shift of the spec's daily multiplier over 2017-10-02..2026-09-17 by k drawn from {-756..-63} U {63..756}, 50 fixed seeds

sources.core_claim: Journal of Asset Management 25(5):493-507 (2024), DOI 10.1057/s41260-024-00376-x. Online 2-state jump model on DD(hl10), Sortino(hl20, hl60), 3000-day training refit every six months, jump penalty chosen monthly by the 0/1 strategy's 8-year validation Sharpe, one-day delay, 10 bp: S&P 500 1990-2023 Sharpe 0.48 -> 0.68, MDD -55.2% -> -26.6%, turnover 44%, average exposure 80%; HMM 0.54, turnover 141%.
sources.project_applicability: Reproduction target (Stage 2a) and the base protocol for every JM specification.
sources.reflection: Authors' own data (Bloomberg total return, GFD 3-month bills); no comparison with volatility targeting; selecting the penalty on validation Sharpe can overfit the validation window. sources.core_claim: Sparse jump-model regimes per factor index drive a dynamic allocation across seven US long-only indices, test 2007-2024 with 5 bp, improving on the market and on equal weight.
sources.project_applicability: Out-of-sample use of the same persistence machinery on factor sleeves, the closest published analogue of gating our ETF sleeves.

sources.core_claim: Authors' Apache-2.0 library: loss = 0.5 * squared Euclidean distance; DP values[t] = loss[t] + min(values[t-1] + penalty); online labels = argmin of forward values; k-means++ starts with n_init 10, max_iter 1000, tol 1e-8; states sorted by cumulative return.
sources.project_applicability: Faithful implementation (P-1 item 2) and the cross-check of our module.

sources.core_claim: Regime-based asset allocation with HMMs can beat static allocation when regimes are persistent and inferred online; the gain depends on persistence and on transaction costs.
sources.project_applicability: Background for the HMM point on the model axis and the role of persistence.

sources.core_claim: Journal of Financial Economics 138 (2020) 95-117: out of sample, volatility-managed versions of most of 103 equity strategies do not beat the unmanaged ones, but momentum strategies improve.
sources.project_applicability: The exposure-matched volatility target is a non-trivial control for a momentum sleeve such as S3; the regime layer must beat it, not only buy-and-hold.
sources.reflection: US factor portfolios, monthly; not levered ETFs. Snapshot reports/research/intel/sources/regime-cycle-2026-10-04/cederburg-2020-volmanaged-jfe.txt.

sources.core_claim: Momentum crashes are concentrated in panic states after bear markets with high volatility and are partly forecastable; a dynamic strategy using bear-state and volatility forecasts roughly doubles the momentum Sharpe ratio.
sources.project_applicability: Mechanism for state dependence of a momentum rotation such as S3 and for why a bear-and-volatility state can add to a pure volatility target.
sources.reflection: Cross-sectional stock momentum, not ETF rotation. Snapshot reports/research/intel/sources/regime-cycle-2026-10-04/daniel-moskowitz-2016-momentum-crashes.txt.

sources.core_claim: Leveraged ETF compounding depends on return autocorrelation and regime: trends enhance returns, mean reversion and volatility clustering induce underperformance (about 20 years of SPY and QQQ data).
sources.project_applicability: Why removing levered exposure in choppy high-volatility bear regimes could raise S3's Sharpe by more than scaling it down.
sources.reflection: Abstract read; no trading rule tested. Snapshot reports/research/intel/sources/regime-cycle-2026-10-04/arxiv__letf-compounding-regime-2504.20116.txt.

sources.core_claim: Copenhagen Business School MSc thesis (2025): regime-aware factor ETF strategies 2017-2025 delivered higher returns, Sharpe and lower drawdowns than benchmarks, but the observed performance gains lack statistical significance.
sources.project_applicability: Independent recent evidence that effects of this kind are small relative to sampling error in 8-year windows; the power section treats the sleeve thresholds as policy thresholds.

sources.core_claim: On 2016-01..2023-09 the SMA200 and credit-ratio gates on S3 did not beat exposure-matched volatility-target controls (Sharpe 0.78-0.81 vs gates 0.34-0.85) or 18 of 20 circular shifts; single specifications, lagging price trends.
sources.project_applicability: The control and placebo design this stage reuses; the new elements are persistence-penalised online clustering, 30+ years of fitting history and the depth sweep.
sources.reflection: Shallow single-spec test under the owner's 10-04 depth rule; it cannot refute the regime layer.

hypothesis.statement: A persistence-penalised online jump model on market risk features identifies equity bear regimes early enough that removing S3's levered exposure in them raises S3's stress-period Sharpe by at least 0.10 over an exposure-matched volatility target, without costing more than 0.10 of recent Sharpe.
hypothesis.failure_mode: S3's monthly momentum rotation and its 0.40 volatility target already shrink exposure in the same episodes, so the jump model adds only what a tighter volatility target adds; or the one-day delay and V-shaped rebounds (2020-04, 2025-04) make the gate re-enter late; or the paper does not reproduce on CRSP value-weighted data.
hypothesis.measurement: Index level: Sharpe, return, volatility, MDD, Calmar, ES 5%, turnover, average exposure and changes per year for buy-and-hold, each spec and its exposure-matched volatility target (1990-2023; 2010-01..2026-07). Sleeves: per object, spec, offset and window the same metrics plus ES97.5, differences to the volatility target and to the ungated sleeve with paired stationary-bootstrap intervals, placebo percentiles, 20 bp, zero delay and a crash-episode table.
hypothesis.stop_pivot: Mechanical status for S3: shadow_candidate_selected, increment_not_robust or no_increment_all_depth_points. The last reads 'no increment at any depth point; underpowered to refute' unless the reproduction passed and power is adequate (plan v2 P-1). Shadow = 8-12 weeks log-only before any allocation change.
